Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities,

FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the 
Surgical Dressings Sectional Committee had been approved by the Medical Equipment and Hospital 
Planning Division Council. 

The first-aid kits specified in this standard are applicable for general use. Although, some industrial 
and commercial first-aid requirements may be met by this kit but the kit is generally not applicable 
for providing specialized first-aid treatment. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the 
final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised). 9 The number of 
significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in 
this standard.

IS 13115 : 1991 



Indian Standard 



PORTABLE FIRST-AID KIT 
FOR GENERAL USE — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard specifies the contents of portable 
first-aid kit intended for providing immediate and 
effective first-aid treatment of common injuries. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

IS No. Title 

3392 : 1965 Anaesthetic airways 

4513 : 1968 Scissors, surgical dressing and 
stitch 

4605 : 1981 Crepe bandage (first revision ) 

4717 : 1980 Zinc oxide self-adhesive plaster 
(first revision ) 

4798 : 1968 Safety pins 

9738 : 1981 Polyethylene bags for general 
purpose 

10637: 1983 Forceps, 
pattern 

11163:1985 



splinter, Arthur's 
First-aid dressings 



3 CONTENTS OF FIRST-AID KIT AND 
QUALITY REQUIREMENTS 

Subject to the other requirements of this standard 
the first-aid kit shall contain each item in minimum 
quantities as specified in Table 1. Each item shall 
conform to the relevant Indian Standard or mono- 
graphs of Indian Pharmacopoeia (IP), British 
Pharmacopoeia ( BP ) 9 or United States Pharma- 
copoeia ( USP ) as given in Table 1. 

4 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION 

In addition to the contents specified in Table 1 
each first aid-kit shall contain the following 



additional information: 

a) Name of contents quantity and other infor- 
mation as set out in Table 1 and a clearly 
printed instructions to immediately replace 
expended contents. 

b) A booklet giving detailed instructions on 
first-aid treatment brought out by the Indian 
Red Cross Society and Saint John's Ambul- 
ance Association and Brigade. 

5 PACKING 

Each first-aid kit shall be packed in a durable 
container such that each item of contents is easily 
accessible. Care shall be taken to ensure that the 
material from which the container is fabricated is 
suitable for the environment for which the kit is 
intended with respect to the possible effect of 
ambient temperature and humidity on deteriora- 
tion of any of the contents. 

6 MARKING 

6.1 Each item of the first-aid kit excluding safety 
pins, scissors and forceps, shall bear on its label 
the following information: 

a) Name of the item and its brand name, if any; 

b) Batch/Lot No. and date of manufacture; 

c) Size/quantity; and 

d) Manufacturing licence No. ( where appli- 
cable ), and manufacturer's name and 
address. 

6.2 The container of first-aid kit shall be legibly 
and indelibly marked with the following inform- 
ation: 

a) Words 'FIRST-AID KIP, in letters not less 
than 20 mm in height; 



b) First-aid symbol; and 

c) Trade-mark, if any, 
name and address. 



and manufacturer's 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standard! 

BIS it a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indim Standards Act, 1986 to . 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if any, are 
issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of 
the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving the 
following reference: 

Doc: No. MHD1S (2113)
